section_title: How does Melchizedek’s story point toward Christ?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 1 This Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him, 2 and Abraham apportioned to him a tenth of everything. First, his name means “king of righteousness.” Then also, “king of Salem” means “king of peace.” 3 Without father or mother or genealogy, without beginning of days or end of life, like the Son of God, he remains a priest for all time.

context_lines: The writer returns to Melchizedek, introduced in [Genesis 14:18–20](https://biblehub.com/bsb/genesis/14.htm). He is both king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He blesses Abraham, who gives him a tenth of the plunder.

Hebrews draws significance from his name and kingdom: righteousness and peace. It also draws attention to the way he appears in Scripture without a recorded family line, birth or death. Those features form a comparison with the Son’s enduring priesthood.

The word [translated like](https://biblehub.com/greek/871.htm) describes being made similar. The passage directs us to the Son through the comparison. It does not supply an unrecorded biography or a list of earlier priests from whom Melchizedek inherited his office.
common_interpretation_lines: [Calvin](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/calvin/hebrews/7.htm), [Wesley](https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-epistle-to-the-hebrews/) and the [USCCB notes](https://bible.usccb.org/bible/hebrews/7) understand the missing family and life records as part of the scriptural portrayal which points to Christ. They do not take their absence as proof that the historical king had no human parents. Wesley expressly distinguishes the unrecorded death of Melchizedek from Christ’s actual enduring life.
god_plan_lines: [Psalm 110:1–4](https://biblehub.com/bsb/psalms/110.htm) brings royal authority and enduring priesthood together. Hebrews itself applies that priestly promise to Jesus. Melchizedek’s earlier appearance therefore belongs to a connection Scripture makes, rather than an identity that must be supplied from speculation.

[Colossians 1:19–20](https://biblehub.com/bsb/colossians/1.htm) describes peace made through Christ’s cross. The king-priest picture finds its fullest significance in the One whose righteous rule and saving work bring people into peace with God.
current_position_lines: Our study [Who Shepherds the Church?](https://thewayofscripture.com/studies/who-shepherds-the-church.html) reads the absence of Melchizedek’s recorded genealogy and succession as part of Scripture’s picture of Christ’s lasting priesthood. The study emphasizes a priesthood that does not depend on a human family line passing a mediating office from generation to generation.

editorial_review.position_source_detail: Who Shepherds the Church? — What Changed at the Cross, lines 44–46; explicit Hebrews 7:1–3 application.
